findings.reason: without a stated rule for which profile's age the median carries and what "no profile younger than the bound" means when an own-records wall is present, the node must invent the contract or ship a figure whose stated age/null behaviour the mechanism cannot produce.
findings.text: the deliverable says "the expected-wait figure Jev is shown carries the age of the profile it was computed from, and reads null when no profile younger than the bound exists", but that figure is `local_lane`'s `expected_wait_s` (`reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:740`), returned by `_expected_wait` (`lane_context.py:616`), which takes a median across every distinct live owner: the pick's own project contributes through in-memory `records` (no persisted profile and no cache age at all, lane_context.py:662-674), and each foreign owner contributes its own separately-cached profile, so there is no single "profile it was computed from", and its existing `None` is returned only when no owning group matched, not when every profile is older than the 24-hour bound. The profile's age itself is also undefined by the plan: the entry written through `capabilities.cached_pick_input_rekeyed` carries only `{version, key, value}` (`reckon/capabilities.py:1319`, `_write_pick_entry` at 1244), so no persisted write-time exists to read an age from.

findings.reason: the fix rests on the well-supported synchronous-rebuild cause and the pick-bound figure; only the strength of this justifying clause would change, not the mechanism or its measure.
findings.text: §27 states "15.3% of the joined picks exceeded the 5 s dispatch bound and fell to the deterministic default", but the cited source measures only that 15.31% of picks' own elapsed time exceeds the bound and explicitly warns that "the dispatcher also performs work before `pick()`; this log cannot predict its actual fallback rate from the pick duration alone" (`docs/research/the-pick-state-render-is-slow-because.html`, proposal section).
